findings.title: All failed attempts return None instead of re-raising
findings.criterion_ref: Criterion 3: “Re-raise the last exception if every attempt fails. It must NOT return None silently.”
findings.trigger: fn() raises on every permitted call.
findings.consequence: retry() falls out of the loop and returns None, so callers cannot distinguish total failure from a successful None result.
findings.evidence: The except block only calls time.sleep(...); after `for i in range(attempts)` finishes, there is no `raise` statement.

findings.title: Backoff is applied after the final attempt
findings.trigger: fn() raises on the final permitted call and backoff is nonzero.
findings.consequence: The caller incurs an unnecessary final delay even though no subsequent attempt will occur.
findings.evidence: `time.sleep(backoff * (2 ** i))` executes unconditionally in every caught-exception path, including when `i == attempts - 1`.

reasoning: The success return and exponential delays preceding retries are implemented, but the all-fail path necessarily violates exception propagation and also sleeps when there is no next attempt. Both directly defeat stated criteria and meet the blocker definition.
